headline: Margins rebound as one-off prior-year charge fades
summary_short: Revenue slipped 1.5% y/y to $311.4 million on unfavorable Protein Sciences mix, but net income more than doubled to $51.0 million and diluted EPS rose to $0.32 from $0.14 as SG&A fell 28% and the effective tax rate dropped to 28.3% from 41.0% a year ago.
summary_long: Organic revenue fell 2% on unfavorable Protein Sciences volume/mix, partly offset by Diagnostics and Spatial Biology strength; FX added 2 points, a divested business subtracted 2 points. Gross margin slipped to 66.9% from 67.9% on mix. The y/y profit surge is mostly a base effect: SG&A fell 28% to $109.3 million because the prior-year quarter carried a non-recurring arbitration-award charge, and the tax rate normalized to 28.3% from 41.0%. Protein Sciences margin fell to 44.2%; Diagnostics and Spatial Biology margin rose to 12.1% on the Exosome divestiture. Cash rose to $209.8 million; no Q3 buybacks; dividend held at $0.08/share. Guides remainder-of-FY2026 capex to ~$7 million, ex-discrete tax rate to 25%-29%.

drivers.explanation: Reported profit growth is largely a base effect: the prior-year quarter's SG&A included a non-recurring arbitration award, and its tax rate was elevated by discrete items; both reversed this quarter.

Organic revenue fell 2% on unfavorable volume and product mix in Protein Sciences, partly offset by Diagnostics and Spatial Biology strength; FX added 2 points, a held-for-sale business subtracted 2 points.
Gross margin fluctuation was primarily a result of changes in product mix, per the filing.
SG&A fell 28% to $109.3M mainly due to the prior year's non-recurring arbitration award and ongoing cost management; R&D fell 5% to $23.5M.
Beyond the operating income gain, the effective tax rate fell to 28.3% from 41.0%, which the filing attributes to the mix of discrete tax items in each period.
Nine-month operating cash flow rose to $196.7M from $189.4M on higher net earnings; no share repurchases occurred in fiscal 2026 versus $175.7M in the prior-year nine months.
